correctness.rationale: The star-coordinate construction gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, each nonsingleton part needs a coordinate attaining distance 2; the tree four-point condition prevents one coordinate serving two such parts. With exactly those coordinates, every singleton must be the unique midpoint of each realized within-part geodesic, so two singleton vertices have zero distance in all coordinates, forcing one extra coordinate. Complete graphs give the q=0 boundary.
